description:
Several safe kernel function-pointer types in `gf2-kernels-simd` reach undefined behaviour when a safe caller violates a length or shape condition that the kernel only debug-asserts; a safe boundary validates, and a caller-trusted path is a distinct `_unchecked` item.

## Background

The kernel crate publishes safe `fn` pointer types whose AVX2 implementations index or load without a release-mode check: `SmallPrimeSpmmRowFn` and `MediumPrimeSpmmRowFn` (the column bound `a_cols[h] * b_stride + n <= b.len()`), `SmallPrimePlePanelBaseFn` and `MediumPrimePlePanelBaseFn` (window shape, inverse-table length, canonical entries indexing the inverse table), `BipedalBinaryKernelFn`, `BipedalUnaryKernelFn` and the F_5 and F_7 kernel types (equal lengths that are a multiple of four). Each type's rustdoc and each call's `// SAFETY:` comment name the caller condition, so shipped callers stay in bounds, but the types are safe, and the repository's convention for a path that skips validation is a separate method under the `_unchecked` name with its precondition documented.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A committed inventory lists every safe kernel entry point of the crate whose soundness depends on a caller condition that release builds do not check.
- [hard] REQ-02: For each listed entry point, either the safe item checks its conditions and panics on violation, or the unchecked path is an `unsafe` or `_unchecked` item with the precondition under Safety and every caller discharging it with a `// SAFETY:` comment; no safe item reaches undefined behaviour for any argument values.
- [hard] REQ-03: One shared test per kernel interface exercises the violated conditions over every implementation and observes a panic or a compile-time-enforced contract, and the shared behavioural suites pass with and without the `simd` feature on Rust 1.95.
- [hard] REQ-04: A choice that adds a release-mode check on a measured hot path carries before/after evidence under the measurement contract, or records the measured cost as accepted.

## Notes

Found while stating the kernel crate's safety contracts. The choice between checking and an unsafe signature per interface is a design decision with performance consequences; the affected kernels serve the prime-field and bipedal paths as well as GF(2).
title: Make caller-trusted safe kernel entry points checked or unchecked by name
